topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the complement system and frames the scope and challenges of the lecture.

topics.label: Fundamentals and nomenclature of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational concepts, nomenclature conventions, and core C3 activation mechanism of the complement system.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three distinct biochemical pathways that initiate complement activation and converge on C3 convertases.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the primary downstream effector functions through which activated complement destroys pathogens and drives inflammation.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how host cells utilize regulatory proteins to prevent complement activation from causing self-damage.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the distinct clinical presentations and disease pathologies resulting from deficiencies in specific complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the mechanisms employed by pathogens to evade complement-mediated immune destruction.

topics.label: Lecture closing
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the complement lecture and previews the upcoming session on the adaptive immune system.
